newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. police hunt for bodies of missing teens.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. police hunt for bodies of missing teens.

text.p: State police and forest rangers were searching Wednesday for the scattered remains of two high school cheerleaders believed to have been murdered in their small upstate New York town.
A neighbour, John Andrews, 31, was being held without bail on kidnapping charges. Police said they believe the girls are dead but do not have enough evidence to charge Andrews with murder.
Sarah Hajney of McLean, New York, and Jennifer Buduc of nearby Dryden, New York, both 16, were reported missing last Friday when they did not show up for school.
Police said they have been finding human remains in variuos locations in rural Chenango and Madison counties, and 60 state troopers and forest rangers were searching those areas Wednesday.
The girls' remains are believed to be scattered over a three- to four-mile area, police said. The region is about 30 miles east of where the girls lived.
Andrews, a computer lathe operator, was arrested late Tuesday. He has refused to help authorities with the search.
The suspect spent more than three years in prison and was dishonourably discharged from the U.S. Air Force in 1994 after he burglarized an apartment and assaulted a woman with a barbell.
A year ago he purchased a house in Sarah Hajney's neighbourhood. On a poignant note, the girl was born in that house, which was built by her grandfather.
Authorities have not said whether they have determined a motive in the case.
